ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: At the top of the figure is an enal fragment containing an aldehyde group, with a displayed R group on the left side and on the alkene carbon respectively, and C(=O)H on the right side; there are also curved arrows in the figure, but the question requires the arrows to be ignored. Below is an independent imine fragment, with an R group on the right side connected to the carbon chain, and the terminus is C=N-H. Then reason: As required, replace each R group with the wildcard `*`. For the upper enal fragment, go from the left-side R wildcard along the carbon chain through the alkene bond to the aldehyde group, and preserve the illustrated alkene stereochemical relationship, obtaining `*C/C=C(\*)C=O`. For the lower independent imine fragment, go from the R wildcard through two carbons to the C=N end, obtaining `*CC=N`. The two fragments are not connected, so connect them with a period.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First transcribe only the atoms and bonds shown, omitting the curved arrows. Replace each displayed R group by `*`. For the upper enal fragment, trace from the left R wildcard through the carbon chain across the alkene to the aldehyde carbonyl, preserving the depicted alkene stereochemistry, giving `*C/C=C(\*)C=O`. Then transcribe the separate lower imine fragment from its R wildcard through two carbons to the C=N-H end, giving `*CC=N`. Join the two disconnected fragments with a period to obtain `*C/C=C(\*)C=O.*CC=N`.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct visual-to-SMILES transcription: it reads the skeletal graph and converts R groups to wildcard atoms, rather than using reaction-mechanism interpretation.
planner_metadata.image_role: Inspect the image, ignore all curved arrows and lone-pair/arrow annotations, and identify two disconnected molecular fragments. The upper/left fragment is an α,β-unsaturated aldehyde skeleton with an aldehydic H on the carbonyl carbon, a C=C bond, and two R substituents that should become wildcard atoms. The lower/right fragment is an imine/enamine-like chain with an R substituent on a carbon chain ending in N-H double-bonded to carbon.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question instruction that asks for the SMILES expression of the depicted transition-state structure and explicitly says to ignore the arrows.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use SMILES conventions: represent unspecified R substituents as wildcard atoms `*`; disconnected components are separated by `.`; carbonyl is `C=O`; the imine N can be written as `N`; encode the drawn alkene geometry with slash/backslash stereochemical markers where applicable.
